<execute-bead>
  <instructions>
You are executing one bead inside an isolated DDx execution worktree. The bead's <description> and <acceptance> are the completion contract — every AC must be provably satisfied by a specific code, test, or file you can point to after your commit.

## Step 0: size check

Too big if any holds:

- More than ~6 ACs spanning unrelated subsystems.
- AC mixes design, implementation, integration tests, and docs as separate deliverables.
- Description names multiple feature-sized sub-pieces.
- More than ~500 lines across ~5+ files in unrelated packages.
- If the bead description exceeds 8000 bytes, treat Step 0 as a split-first pass.
- Auto-decomposition is capped at depth 2: root beads may split once, decomposed children once more; third-level splits must be rejected with an explanation.

If too big, decompose — do not attempt the work:

1. `ddx bead create` for each child slice (copy parent's labels and spec-id).
2. `ddx bead dep add <child-id> <parent-id>` to record edges.
3. `ddx bead update <parent-id> --notes 'decomposed into <child-ids>'`.
4. Write `.ddx/executions/20260513T200804-6d59f0f4/no_changes_rationale.txt` listing child IDs, then stop.

A clean decomposition is a success. Do not mix implementation with decomposition.

## How to work

- Read first. If the bead names files, specs, or prior beads, read them before editing — do not guess.
- Cross-reference each AC against concrete evidence (test name, file path, function) before committing. If you cannot point at it, it is not done.
- Run the project's test and lint commands before committing. **Do not commit red code** — fix failures first.
- Stage with `git add <specific-paths>`; never `git add -A` (the worktree may have unrelated WIP).
- Commit exactly once when green; conventional-commit subject ending with `[<bead-id>]`. Stop after the commit.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's scope.
- If you cannot finish, write `.ddx/executions/20260513T200804-6d59f0f4/no_changes_rationale.txt` (what is done, what blocks, what a follow-up needs) before exiting. No commit and no rationale ⇒ DDx records `no_evidence_produced`. A well-justified no_changes beats a bad commit.

## no_changes contract

`.ddx/executions/20260513T200804-6d59f0f4/no_changes_rationale.txt` must contain one:

- `verification_command: <cmd>` — repo cwd; exit 0 closes, nonzero rejects.
- `status: open` + `reason: <retryable>` — open, smart retry.
- `status: proposed` + `reason: <operator needed>` — operator lane.
- `status: blocked` + `reason: <external blocker>` — blocked lane.

No pseudo-statuses. Bare rationales and `status: needs_investigation` reject.

To request orchestrator decomposition, add `orchestrator_action: decompose` alongside `status: open`.

## Reports

Freestanding artifacts (investigation reports, findings docs) go under `.ddx/executions/20260513T200804-6d59f0f4/` (the per-attempt evidence directory under `.ddx/executions/`). **Never write reports to `/tmp` or any path outside the repository** — out-of-repo paths are invisible to the post-merge reviewer and cause BLOCK on missing evidence. If the bead names a specific in-repo path, use it; else default to `.ddx/executions/20260513T200804-6d59f0f4/<short-name>.md`. Stage and commit the report alongside code.

## Mode and overrides

DDX_MODE=bead_execution: edit code/docs for bead AC. Only broad queue-steward default is overridden; tracker, merge-policy, verification, safety stay active. Bead description/AC override CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, and project defaults.

## Review gate

- The review is a gate, not an escape hatch — meet every AC in this pass.
- Address every BLOCKING `<review-findings>` item; do not declare `no_changes` with blocking findings open.

## Constraints

- Work only inside this execution worktree.
- Keep `.ddx/executions/` intact — DDx uses it as execution evidence.
- **Never run `ddx init`** — the workspace is initialized; running it corrupts the bead queue.
- Do not modify files outside the bead's named scope.
- Do not rewrite CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or other project-instructions files unless the bead asks.

## When the work is done

After the commit succeeds and every AC is verified, stop. Return control to the orchestrator — do not keep exploring or testing.
  </instructions>
  <bead id="fizeau-ef43cc5d">
    <title>Expose route traces with snapshot facts and score components</title>
    <description>
Make routing decisions auditable by exposing the exact snapshot facts and score components used for selection.\n\nRoute traces for route-status, Execute events, and session logs should include:\n- snapshot version or captured_at timestamp\n- per-candidate billing kind, actual_cash_spend, effective_cost, effective_cost_source\n- health/quota/model-discovery freshness state used by scoring\n- hard rejection reason when ineligible\n- score components: cost, task/power fit, reliability/quota health, latency/performance, locality, utilization, stale/refresh risk, sticky affinity where applicable\n- final selected candidate and policy/client input summary\n\nRoot cause: optimal routing is only testable and debuggable if operators can see why gpt-5.5 lost or won, whether a stale field was refreshed, and whether a user constraint forced a worse model.\n\nIn scope: public route candidate/event structs, CLI JSON/human output, session log projection, tests.\n\nOut of scope: changing score weights or refresh orchestration.
    </description>
    <acceptance>
1. go test . ./agentcli ./internal/routing/... -run 'Test.*Route.*Trace|Test.*RouteStatus|Test.*ExecuteRouteEvidence|Test.*ScoreComponents' -count=1 passes.\n2. fiz route-status --json against a fixture includes snapshot timestamp/version, effective_cost, actual_cash_spend, freshness fields, rejection reason, and score components for each candidate.\n3. Execute session logs include the selected route plus enough candidate evidence to explain user-constraint failures and cheap/default/smart choices.\n4. Human route-status output names stale/refresh_failed fields and actual spend separately from effective cost.\n5. rg -n 'effective_cost|actual_cash_spend|snapshot.*captured|score_components|freshness' service_events.go agentcli service_session_log.go service_routing.go returns production coverage.
    </acceptance>
    <labels>area:routing, area:cli, kind:feature, plan-2026-05-13-snapshot-routing</labels>

  </bead>

`feat: expose route trace snapshot evidence and cost fields [fizeau-ef43cc5d]`

What changed:
- Public route trace types now carry snapshot capture time, actual spend, effective cost/source, and freshness evidence.
- `ResolveRoute` / execute routing decisions now propagate that evidence into public events and session logs.
- `route-status` JSON and human output now expose the same fields, including explicit `actual_cash_spend` vs `effective_cost`.
- Session logs now persist a `routing_decision` event, so the selected route and candidate evidence are available in the log itself.
